name: reps-rtc-spike
symbols_from_why: Runs against the PINNED BASE ROM: every symbol it reads is vanilla.
description: `reps` SLICE 1 RTC SPIKE -- an OBSERVATION, not a feature test. scope.md folds it into slice 1 deliberately, to buy the answer to slice 2's one genuine unknown a slice early: can a real-RTC countdown be verified headlessly at all? mGBA derives the emulated RTC from host wall-clock time, so a headless run at many times real speed may see almost no real seconds pass -- which would make a 60-second timed set cost 60 real seconds per seed and be hostile to a 4-seed spec. This spec needs NO code change: gLocalTime is an engine global (struct Time { s16 days; s8 hours; s8 minutes; s8 seconds; }) that src/rtc.c fills in. It samples that global across a long cold-boot run and simply records what it does. The assertions below deliberately assert only that the machine was alive and the read was valid -- the ANSWER is in the printed sample table, not in a PASS. A spike that asserted a specific RTC rate would be asserting the host's clock, which is not a property of the ROM.

probes.why: gLocalTime as raw bytes -- days (s16), hours, minutes, seconds. Sampled densely across 3600 frames (~60 s of EMULATED time at 60 fps) so the relationship between emulated frames and RTC seconds is visible directly in the table rather than inferred.
gLocalTime.seconds (offset 4) on its own, so a change is legible at a glance in the sample list.
gMain.vblankCounter1. Establishes how many frames actually elapsed, which is the denominator of the whole question.

gMain.callback2. Records WHERE the game was during the observation -- src/rtc.c's RtcCalcLocalTime() is driven from the overworld, so which callback was running decides whether gLocalTime was being refreshed at all. Without this the sample table would be uninterpretable.

assert.why: The global was readable at every sample. Weak by doc 55 sec.9.4's classification, and deliberately so: this spec's job is to MEASURE, and a spike that manufactured a strong assertion about the host's clock would be asserting the wrong machine.
3600 frames really elapsed. This is the load-bearing assertion here -- it is what makes the recorded RTC samples a measurement rather than a snapshot.
Every non-null callback resolves in this build's own .sym, so the recorded location of the game is a name and not a number.
